ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Srinivasa Ramanujan Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: New patient with four weeks of evening fevers and night sweats, weight loss and right upper quadrant pain, in a 29-year-old mathematician from Tamil Nadu who came to a research fellowship here three years ago. Concerns: He is afraid he has tuberculosis and wants to know what is wrong; He wants to keep working on his mathematics while he is treated; He wants any food and medicine advice to fit his diet and his tradition; He feels alone here and misses his family. [S]

tr.td: Metronidazole 250 mg oral tablet, three tablets (750 mg) three times a day with food for 10 days
Three tablets every 8 hours with food for 10 days
Paromomycin 250 mg oral capsule, two capsules (500 mg) three times a day with meals for 7 days, started the day after metronidazole ends
Two capsules every 8 hours with meals for 7 days
Vitamin B12 (cyanocobalamin) 1,000 microgram oral tablet, one tablet daily
Cholecalciferol 50,000 unit (1.25 mg) oral tablet, one tablet once a week for 8 weeks
One tablet once a week for 8 weeks
Cholecalciferol 2,000 unit (50 microgram) oral tablet, one tablet daily, from the end of the weekly course
Rifampin 300 mg oral capsule, two capsules (600 mg) once daily on an empty stomach for 4 months
Two capsules each morning before breakfast for 4 months

Weight loss of 5 kg over two months (57 to 52 kg), with poor appetite: resolved, confirmed [S]

Latent tuberculosis infection: positive interferon-gamma release assay, normal lungs on the radiograph, three sputum smears, NAAT and cultures negative; treated with four months of rifampin: active, confirmed [S]
Adjustment disorder with depressed mood (PHQ-9 12, no thoughts of self-harm) during a serious illness, far from his wife and family: active, confirmed [S]
Acute viral upper respiratory infection, three weeks into rifampin and six weeks after treatment of the liver abscess, without signs of abscess relapse; resolved: resolved, confirmed [S]

list.item: Mathematician holding a research fellowship at a university here; came from Tamil Nadu three years ago; before that a clerk in a port office while he worked on mathematics on his own; works long hours, often through the night [S]
Lives alone in a college room with a small kitchen; married, and his wife lives with his parents in India; calls home rarely and letters are slow; few friends here who share his language or food [S]

Strict lacto-vegetarian by his tradition: rice, lentils and other pulses, vegetables, fruit, milk, curd and ghee; no meat, fish or eggs; cooks for himself, prefers food prepared by himself or within his tradition, and in recent weeks has cooked only once a day or less; finds few of his foods in local shops [S]
Tobacco: never. Alcohol: never, by his tradition. No drug use [S]
Hindu; prays daily; his faith and his mathematics matter most to him [S]
Stipend from his fellowship; student health insurance; no car; walks everywhere [S]
Prefers to be addressed as Mr. Ramanujan; explains that Srinivasa is his father's name and that he has no family name [S]

Results of the abdominal ultrasound, serology and tuberculosis tests, with an infectious diseases consultation, and start of treatment
Day 12: end of metronidazole and start of paromomycin, blood count, CRP and liver tests, mood and safety review
Six weeks: recovery, final sputum cultures, liver tests before rifampin, vitamin B12, mood, influenza vaccine
Three months: abscess treatment complete, rifampin month two, blood count, liver tests, vitamins, mood, and plans to visit home
Same-day sick visit for a cold with fever, and the question of an abscess relapse
Periodic adult preventive visit with pre-travel advice

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Infectious diseases consultation at the second visit for fever, weight loss and right upper quadrant pain in a young man from South India with a history of dysentery, to interpret the tuberculosis and amebiasis tests, the imaging, and the choice and order of treatment

Tuberculosis evaluation before any antibiotic: chest radiograph, three induced sputum samples for acid-fast smear, NAAT and mycobacterial culture, an interferon-gamma release assay, and HIV testing; airborne precautions until three smears are negative
Liver and gut evaluation: abdominal ultrasound tomorrow morning, Entamoeba histolytica serology, stool antigen or PCR and microscopy, two sets of blood cultures, liver tests and CRP
Nutrition: vitamin B12, folate, ferritin and 25-hydroxyvitamin D measured; weight at every visit; a dietitian visit to plan meals within his vegetarian diet and his rules

Mood and safety: PHQ-9 and GAD-7 at intake and at least monthly while symptoms last; structured safety assessment and a written safety plan with the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline; safety reviewed at every visit; short-term counseling with the university counseling service, at times he chooses

Support far from home: the university's international student office and his department's graduate office about leave and deadlines while he is ill; a regular time to call his family; introductions, at his wish, to the local Tamil association and a Hindu temple community with shared meals; a letter for his fellowship about his illness
Acetaminophen for fever and pain, no more than 3 g a day; nothing else until the results are known
Cold: rest, fluids, warm salt-water gargles, honey in warm water and acetaminophen; continue rifampin; no antibiotic; return for fever over three days, right upper quadrant pain, or breathlessness

As the infectious diseases physician advised: metronidazole 750 mg three times a day for 10 days, then paromomycin 500 mg three times a day for 7 days, not taken together; no aspiration unless fever persists after 72 hours, the abscess grows, or rupture threatens; a nurse phone check on the third day; no repeat imaging if he recovers

Vitamin B12 1,000 micrograms by mouth daily and vitamin D 50,000 units weekly for 8 weeks, then 2,000 units daily; a dietitian plan within his rules: protein from dal, chickpeas, beans, milk, curd and paneer; dairy and fortified foods for B12; batch cooking once a day for two meals; easy foods such as curd rice and khichdi on tired days; an Indian grocery delivery

Latent tuberculosis infection, once cultures were negative and the liver tests normal: rifampin 600 mg daily for 4 months, with a monthly clinical check for nausea, rash, jaundice and adherence; liver tests at baseline and at two months because of the recent liver disease; orange body fluids explained
A diagnosis within days, with tuberculosis either confirmed or excluded before any treatment that could hide it
Amebic liver abscess diagnosed at the second visit; active tuberculosis excluded by the radiograph, three smears, NAAT and cultures at six weeks
No fever, the abscess treated, and the luminal course completed
Afebrile by the third day of metronidazole; paromomycin completed; CRP and liver tests normal
Regain at least half of the lost weight within three months, on a diet that keeps his rules
52.0 to 56.6 kg, nearly all the weight lost
Vitamin B12 and vitamin D in the normal range and the anemia resolved
B12 520 pg/mL; 25-hydroxyvitamin D 32 ng/mL; hemoglobin 13.8 g/dL
PHQ-9 below 10 with no thoughts of self-harm, and regular contact with people who matter to him
PHQ-9 12 to 5; weekly calls home and a weekly meal with others from his community
Complete four months of rifampin for latent tuberculosis infection
Month two of four; no side effects; liver tests normal

list.item: Independent in daily activities, but tired by afternoon, cooking less, and has missed some seminars in the last two weeks [S]

Quiet and courteous, thoughtful, with soft speech and some slowing; mood low and worried; affect constricted but brightens when he talks about his work; thought clear and logical; no thoughts of self-harm; PHQ-9 12, GAD-7 9 [S]

text.paragraph: Structured synthetic safety assessment on 1917-01-12: current ideation absent, intent absent, plan absent. Outpatient care with close follow-up. He has no thoughts of suicide or self-harm now and has had none. Because he is ill, isolated, far from home and screening in the moderate range, his risk factors were reviewed with him privately and a written safety plan was made: his warning signs (not sleeping, not eating, not wanting to see anyone), what helps, who he can call, and the clinic number. The 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline was given and saved in his phone. Lethal-means counseling: no firearm; medicines dispensed in short supplies. Safety reviewed at every visit [S]
